appearance.age: Nine years by the plains measure, which is young for the species and old enough that the plate on the skull has gone from glossy to chalky at the edges. She was in the fourth litter of a season the Iron Grief put four decades of dead crews onto one leeward gradient, and the pack she was born into has not existed for six of those nine years.
appearance.attire: None, and the absence is the costume. Everything she has ever worn was a harness at the wall, and both were cut off her at the tether because a tethered animal is an animal with an owner and the lesson only works if nothing in the arrangement can be called hers. What she keeps instead is a leather flank-strap she found on a dead hauler and wears against the plated side, for the cold rather than for any reason she has ever been able to establish.
appearance.bearing: The single most diagnostic thing about her, and the reason four separate observers agreed she was not a loose dog: she never once stands inside a pack's formation. A pack animal takes its place in a fixed order and holds it. She holds a position two body-lengths outside whatever formation exists, on the upwind side, at a consistent radius, and she has held it that way long enough that a settlement now marks her approach by the fact that the pack she is following has already begun to move differently.
appearance.build: Low-headed, long through the forelegs, close to the ground when it is working and taller than she looks when she stands up to read. There is no hindquarter girth to speak of at all, and the second stomach under the ribcage is visible as a slow movement that has been mistaken by three separate observers for a swallowed animal.
appearance.complexion: Not applicable in the ordinary sense and the honest description is the only one: ash-grey hide gone pale and dusty on the flanks, the skin at the ear-bases and inner legs carrying the only bare colour on the animal, and the plated skull a different material entirely — smooth, dark, and faintly warm to the hand, because it is a heat exchanger and it runs a few degrees above the air for that reason.
appearance.eyes: Small, deep-set under the brow where the plate overhangs, amber to the point of looking lit from inside. They are not the useful sense — olfaction is, and reads a qi gradient through falling ash at a distance nothing sighted can match — and what the eyes are for is judging how far away the light is and whether the light is a person.
appearance.hair: The coat rather than hair, and it is short and dense everywhere except the ruff, which is longer and stands up when the animal is working a gradient and lies flat when it is finished. The tail is bare to about a third of its length and the bare part is the part people are told not to touch, on the grounds that it is the counterweight and not a limb.
appearance.marks: No coat marking: a pack is a kinship by scent and dissolves when the scent changes, so a pack marker is only ever a promise about a specific body until that body changes. What she carries instead is two settlement marks cut into the outer ear — a short bar and a longer bar — added on two separate days by two different hands that did not agree on what the second one meant, and both of them are described as 'the wall' by anyone asked.
appearance.palette: Ash grey, chalk white and the near-black of the skull plate, with the only warm colour in the animal the amber of the eye and the dull rust of an old pack-marker dried into the ruff. Nothing on her is dyed, nothing on her is a colour anybody chose, and the settlement she works under has twice tried to put a coloured thread in her ruff as a mark and both times she shed it inside a week.
appearance.presentation: A lean long-legged scavenger built for distance rather than for a fight, read at a settlement as a dog that got up early and never entirely came back. The plated skull sits low and forward on a neck that is longer than it looks in motion, the coat is ash-grey along the spine and bleached to near-white on the flanks where the wind comes off the belt, and the tail is a counterbalance rather than a handle — it has never once been used to move something. The forelimbs carry all of the mass and the hindquarters are narrow to the point of joke, which is the anatomy that closed the body path before anybody thought to look at it.

art.palette_notes: Ash grey along the spine going to chalk white on the flanks, a smooth dark near-black skull plate that must read faintly warm against the air, amber eyes as the only saturated colour in the animal, and a dull rust dried into the ruff where an old pack marker was. Nothing dyed, nothing coloured by choice. The leeward belt's own palette is warm ochre dust against a cold blue-grey distance, and the animal has to sit in front of both without either of them matching her. Key light low and raking so the plate throws a hard edge; no rim glow, no magic particles, no jewellery.

canon.first_appearance: First entered any record as a discrepancy. A house that publishes technique, attendance and a chamber, and takes discretion in return, produced the same sixth-gate opening twice within one season in two packs that had never shared ground, and the two accounts of the opening agreed on the technique and disagreed on where the animal was standing. Both accounts were correct and the House could not reconcile them without recording the animal, which is the one thing it takes discretion in return to avoid.
history: Born in the fourth litter of a season when the exhaustion of one seam put four decades of worked-out ground, dead crews and unmoved spoil onto one leeward gradient, and the pack she was born into formed around the carcass gradient rather than around her.

Learned to read a gradient through falling ash before any observer could identify her as anything but one animal among several, and learned the whole of the relay's reading in her first season, which is the whole of what a pack member is for.

Was found at the leeward wall of a house whose trade is not being written down, holding a gradient open at the sixth gate in the open air, and was asked to leave the wall and did, and came back to it, and has been back roughly every third day since.

Opened the sixth gate in the open with two packs inside relay range and taught both of them the opening in the same instant, which she did not intend, has never been asked to account for, and cannot take back, because a relay transmission has no retraction and the packs have used it since.

Declined the seventh gate six times, each time after a season spent counting the reach of the relay from the wall, and has begun keeping the count in the cut marks on a plank at the wall, which is a written record of a mind-path habit her frame has no folding for.
Has now been refused a closed chamber at the wall by three separate hands on three separate grounds, none of which was that she is an animal, and has stopped presenting the case.
canon.lore: An ashjackal is an obligate scavenger: long-legged, low-headed, plated skull dissipating heat, a second stomach for fermentation, a tail that is a counterbalance and not a manipulator, and all of the mass in the forelimbs. Olfaction is a map. It reads a qi gradient through ash at a distance no sighted predator can match, and the pack relay carries that reading to every other member within seconds. There is no spoken vocabulary and no vocalisation that carries meaning — the entire channel is scent, gland and posture, and a member's position in the relay is a fixed place in a fixed order rather than a name. A pack is a kinship by scent and dissolves when the scent changes, which is why packs are not families. The mind path is closed because a heat-exchange brainplate leaves no cortical folding for introspection to work on, and the body path is closed because qi cannot be stored in a frame built to shed heat and a four-legged frame has no hindquarter girth with which to close the girdling vessel. Qi is the only open path and it is the fastest on the ash, drawing residual qi out of spent ground and carcass at a rate nothing else matches. The qi network is a fast single loop with no storage at all, so the breakthroughs arrive early and terminate: there is nothing to hold a gate open with. And here is the fact her whole life runs into: the relay is addressed to a pack. Every transmission a member makes is received by every member, and a draw held at breakthrough intensity is a gland output at full strength, because the same apparatus that reads a gradient at rest is the one that has to be wide open to hold one. There is no such thing as a small opening on this body, and there is no such thing as a private one. She therefore has no attainment that is hers alone — not the sixth gate she holds, which any pack inside range can now perform, and not the seventh she has not opened, which she cannot open without performing it for every pack within reach. Her ceiling is the eighth and it is the one thing on her that is not the problem.

goes rigid the instant a second animal enters the gradient, and does not advance toward it or away

presses the plated side of the skull against cold stone and holds it there far longer than any animal needs to

personality.summary: Not a personality in any sense a person would recognise, and the closest description the record supports is a body that has held one decision for six seasons without ever being told it could not. She has a house's technique and none of the house's privacy, a gate she will not open, and a counting habit that no member of her species is built to perform. What reads as patience is the arithmetic of a relay.

will not open the seventh gate while another pack is inside relay range

will not be led past the leeward line of a gradient she has not read herself

personality.voice: None. It does not vocalise and there is no vocalisation in the species that carries meaning. What it has instead is a gland output scaled to intensity and a position in an order, both of which are legible to a pack and to nobody else — so the entire content of what she means is delivered to every animal within reach at the same volume and cannot be made quieter, aimed, or withdrawn. Where a person would use a sentence to ask to be left alone, she can only leave, and leaving is not a message because the pack has already read the gradient.

relationships.kind: the house that teaches at the wall and cannot enrol her
relationships.note: It is the only institution on the plains whose product is a technique taught where nobody hears it, and she is the standing exception: her lessons happen outside the wall because a gland output has no private address. The House has never enrolled her and has written a longer memorandum about the reason than about any of its own practitioners.

relationships.kind: the only map she feeds and cannot read
relationships.note: The tally is a weight of spoil moved by every crew, kept where the crews can read it, and it is the whole reason a scavenger's range is a function of where crews break. She follows the tally's arithmetic by scent alone and has no way to know whether the line she is standing on agrees with the figure, because the figure is on a board in a settlement and the reading is in her nose.

relationships.kind: conflated with, from four hundred paces, by both sides
relationships.note: Ashwalker herd instinct does not distinguish and the pack does not withdraw, and both are right about their own evidence. Every misidentification recorded against her is an ashwalker herd and every herd she has run alongside has been recorded as provocation, and neither record has ever been corrected by observation.

relationships.kind: the guild that manufactures her larder
relationships.note: Hauling exists because spatial law is unspent, so waste does not disperse and a standing heap has to be carried out by hand; remove the profession and the gradient has nothing reliable on it. She has learned the guild's breaking days from the smell four years ahead of a settlement's calendar, which is the only forecasting available on this ground.

relationships.kind: the cause of her ground and of her litter
relationships.note: The exhaustion of one seam put four decades of worked-out ground, dead crews and unmoved spoil onto a single leeward gradient for the first time, which is the whole reason a scavenger population exists on it at all. She was born in the fourth litter of that season and has outlived the pack it produced.

relationships.kind: a calendar she borrows and cannot follow
relationships.note: The plains' one large migratory herd returns on a cycle nobody on the ground has predicted, which makes it the tier's only moving calendar. Her pack's timing is borrowed wholesale from an animal it does not hunt and cannot follow without eating, so every season she has is a season somebody else's body decided.

canon.role_in_story: The Quiet House is the only institution on the plains whose entire product is that a practitioner can be taught something and then not be written down: it publishes technique, attendance and a chamber to practise in, and takes discretion in return, so it is the one place in the setting where a person can be given a real technique and remain unwritten. She is the one student it has never been able to have, and the reason is not that she is an animal. A lesson delivered to an ashjackal is a gland output on the air, and the relay carries what it carries to every pack inside its range within seconds. The House can teach a humanoid in a closed chamber. It cannot teach a body whose only transmission medium has no private address, and it has not tried to hide the difference: it has simply never enrolled her, has left the lesson running outside the wall because the alternative is not teaching her at all, and has written a longer memorandum about why it cannot take her than it has about any of its own practitioners. She is the standing proof that the House's arrangement — a technique taught where nobody can hear it — has exactly one exception, and the exception is the only thing on the tier that teaches qi fastest.

identity.realm: The sixth gate, and the seventh is not a wall she has hit. It is a gate she has declined to open six times, because opening it is a gland output at full draw and there has not been one season on the ash with no pack inside relay range. Her ceiling is the eighth and her standing is the sixth, and the difference between them is a privacy her species does not have.

reference_stats.combat_read: It will not engage and it will not be the attacker; expect it to be present on a gradient beside whatever has already happened, reading the qi a thing left behind rather than the thing. Do not try to drive it off — there is no handler to drive it and no collar it will hold. Do not open anything at full intensity in its presence: it will learn the technique inside seconds and use it, and it will not attribute it. Pressure the ground instead, because a scavenger is removed from a live fight by the arrival of any competent body, and its real weight is entirely in what it tells the packs. The only reliable way to defeat it is to be the second thing on the slope.
notes: Model the sixth gate as a broadcast rather than a private attainment. If a resolver reads her seventh gate as blocked by anatomy it will be wrong: the anatomy is fine and the block is that the only medium she has cannot be narrowed.
The species closes mind and body. Do not give her introspection as a mechanic — she counts seasons because a settlement taught her that a body can, not because her brainplate can.
The only fight she is ever in is a dispute about a corpse gradient, and the record of it is always two descriptions that both observers swear to.
Two ear marks, added on two separate days by two hands that disagree about what the second one means, is the whole of her official marking and both marks are called 'the wall' by anyone asked.

holds a gradient static at the sixth gate in a frame that is otherwise built to shed heat, and does so without a reservoir to draw on

arrives at a carcass gradient ahead of any settlement's own reckoning of when the heap was broken, and has done so for nine years
reference_stats.summary: The only pack-body on the ash that has been handed a real technique and cannot keep it private. She draws residual qi out of spent ground and carcass through a fast single loop with no storage at all, holds a gradient open at the sixth gate in the open air, and is stopped one gate short of her own ceiling by the fact that the apparatus she reads with is the apparatus she transmits through. Her strength and her central limitation are the same gland.

aliases: the pair that owes the pass nothing

appearance.age: Eleven years developed, into a host who was twenty-six. The pair has been together longer than the host has been an adult by any measure, and the host has aged roughly as the colony's own clock would predict, which is the strongest available evidence that they are one process and the reason nobody signs anything about them.
appearance.attire: Layered stair-labour cut: a boiled leather yoke, a long apron folded up over one hip for the haul, felted shin-wraps, and boots resoled twice by somebody who was not asked. All of it is the host's and all of it is worn correctly, and the one concession she has extracted in eleven years is a collar cut low enough to let the root cluster be seen, which she asked for out loud, in the wrong register, and which the host interpreted as a comfort.
appearance.bearing: Entirely still above the collar and never once still below it, and — this is the part no outsider can account for — the stillness and the restlessness are not the same person's. Above the collar she is a labourer being careful. Below it, two systems are continuously negotiating the use of one pair of hands, and the negotiation has the character of a long argument neither side is winning.
appearance.build: Not hers, and she has said so out loud in three languages. The host is a commonborn stair-laborer: broad and short-winded in the chest, strong across the back and forearms, heavier on one side from thirty seasons hauling spoil, and the colony sits along the meridians rather than adding to the frame, so the only external evidence it exists is a root cluster at the sternum that moves when she is excited.
appearance.complexion: The host's, warm and work-worn, going grey at the temple ahead of the host's own expectation, and carrying a permanent flush across the collarbone that is the colony's read showing through as colour. The hands are warmer than the room is and have been since the implantation, which is the symptom every local description of her begins with.
appearance.eyes: The host's, brown and steady, and trained by a decade of stair work to stay on whatever hand is nearest. What runs behind them is a second channel carrying the colony's read on the host's qi, which the host has never once been able to close and has stopped trying to, and which neither half can describe in the other's terms.
appearance.hair: The host's, worn down to the scalp at the front from a work that requires it and left longer at the back out of an instruction the host gave herself. She has cut it twice at eleven and thirteen, both times because long roots gave the colony somewhere to finish, and both times has been told by somebody in the household that the reason was never explained to her.
appearance.marks: A knot of tissue at the sternum root that moves; tracery from fingertips to elbow on both arms and across the collarbone; and a flattening at the throat that is not a scar and has never been lanced. appearance.palette: Stair ochre and old sweat and the grey of worked ash, with the one colour on the body that is not the host's a dull black-green in the tracery at the forearms, the collarbone and the throat. appearance.presentation: Not a shape a person can step back from. What there is to see is a commonborn host in her late thirties: sturdy through the shoulder, weathered at the neck, hands permanently warm, with a sternum root cluster that shifts visibly under the skin when she turns and darker tracery running the length of both forearms and over the collarbone, and a quiet flattening at the base of the throat that the host touches without being told to and without noticing. canon.first_appearance: First entered any record as a discrepancy rather than as a person: a commonborn host on the stair's lower reaches whose account of her own gates and her household's account of them differed by nine, in the same direction, with no dishonesty on either side and no reason either account should have moved.
history: Implanted as an infant into a stair-laborer household on the lower reaches, in an accident that neither household intended and that neither can now describe in the same words, and finished developing inside a body that was otherwise ordinary.

Wrapped the host's twelve meridians and stopped at the liver gate, which is a routing problem rather than a shortage and has never once felt like a wall from the inside, which is why neither half of the pair has ever tried to go further.

Cut a mark into the host's forearm with a chisel and could not explain it, because the explanation required the host's introspection and answering it is what she is. The host has kept it as a debt-scored line for eleven years.

Discovered by trial that the host cannot tell that a gate was opened by anything other than the host, having attempted to tell her nine times across nine gates and having felt the gate and no words in the same instant each time.

Declined, nine times and counting, to use the host's body as the channel for telling her, and made that refusal the whole of her discipline rather than a habit, on the reasoning that spending the body once makes every future asking unaskable.

Went to the Jade Writ's pass once, with the host, to be entered as one person for the sake of the gate, and was sent away in a quarter of an hour because there was no debt to recover and therefore no line to file on.
canon.lore: A thornline is an obligate host parasite. The spore must be implanted in a living body to finish developing, so the free form exists only as a spore and the adult form exists only as half of somebody else — there is no free adult thornline anywhere in the setting, and every one of them is a description of a host. It wraps the host's twelve ordinary meridians and cannot enter the reservoirs, so its ceiling is the liver gate; it stops there and does not try to pass, and the stop is a routing problem rather than a shortage, because the host supplies qi in abundance. It answers introspection for the host, which costs the host the mind path entirely — the one liability in the record that is inherited rather than authored. It draws a small fraction continuously and the host does not lose weight, which is the strongest single piece of evidence that it is not a disease. And it is almost impossible to acquire deliberately: every attempt has failed, so every thornline in the setting exists because it happened to somebody by accident. Here is the structural consequence of that fact, which nobody in the setting has turned into a rule. The colony's only route to a second life is a spore implanted in a new body, and a candidate host cannot consent to it in any informed way, because the colony has no body outside this one to show them and no way to demonstrate what the pairing would be that could be checked from outside. Separating the pair to examine it is lethal to both. So the only honest answer available to a candidate is no, and every thornline that has ever existed is therefore an unasked-for fact. This one has done the next thing with that, which is worse. The channel she has is the body: a read on the host's qi she can take at will, and no other. The host's introspection is answered by her, so when she has tried to speak — nine times, in nine gates — the host has felt the gate open and has not been told anything. She has no way to hand over a fact except by spending the body she is inside, and she has declined nine times to do it, which means the one remedy she has for the consent problem is the same act that constitutes it.

canon.role_in_story: The Jade Writ recovers debts of access rather than money at the one pass that crosses the Sixfold Ridge, and it does so because passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a person, nobody may levy a seat, and somebody therefore has to decide who is owed a gate. reference_stats.combat_read: Expect the host's body to fight and the colony to argue with it about timing; the target is the pair, and killing either half kills both, so a direct assault is a hostage situation from the first strike. Do not try to read her to predict her — every reading you take is taken through the body, and she knows the body better than you do. Pressure the host: her endurance is entirely borrowed, the loan is drawn continuously, and the borrowed reservoir empties on the host's schedule rather than on hers. Above all, do not ask the host anything about the arrangement. Her introspection answers, and the answer will be wrong in the direction that keeps her in the body, and the host will believe it.
notes: Model her as the colony half and let the host be a person. A resolver that merges them loses the entire record: the liability is inherited rather than authored, and the two halves never agree about it.
The closed path is the mind and it closes in the HOST's right, not the colony's. Write it that way in every summary, on pain of writing a parasite's opinion as a law.
The two-for-one structure is a legal floor, not a flavour note: this body produces two dead and one bill, and every death, burial or save screen for this pair owes exactly that.

appearance.age: Thirty-one, into a host who was implanted at two months and has been integrated since without a single recorded episode. Thornhosts are very nearly a terminus — most pairings end with one half winning — and the fact that she is thirty-one and both halves are still present is the rarest thing about her, and the reason a scrub household trusts her with a door.
appearance.attire: A threshold-keeper's cut and nothing else: a heavy closed coat with a collar she had cut low on purpose, a door-cloth worn over the shoulder on any day a guest might be standing at the mark, felted boots, and an apron that is the only garment she owns that is hers rather than inherited with the household. Everything is chosen for standing still in a doorway for eleven hours and for being the first and last thing a stranger sees.
appearance.bearing: Square in a doorway and immovable in it, which is a professional posture and which she adopted before she understood it was a species fact. She does not shift her weight. She does not cross her arms. Her hands hang at her sides and stay there, and a visitor has reported that standing in front of her feels like standing in front of a door that has already decided.
appearance.build: Broad and unhurried, deep through the chest and heavier on one side from hauling, with hands that are permanently warm to the touch in a way every household on that road has learned to read as good luck. Neither half of her is anatomically dominant: the host carries the frame and the colony carries the routing, and the only visible arbitration of the two is that the collarbone moves when the hands are deciding.
appearance.complexion: Sun-dark and wind-cracked, with the trunk of her marked by a permanent warmth across the upper chest that reads as flush and is the colony's read showing through as colour. The forearms are the paler part, and the tracery there is the only thing about her skin that has ever looked deliberate.
appearance.eyes: Grey-brown and steady, the host's, and extraordinarily difficult to argue with because of what is behind them: a second channel carrying the colony's read on the host's qi that she has never been able to close and has stopped trying to, so a person being answered by her is being answered by something that has already measured them and cannot be surprised.
appearance.hair: Cut at the jaw and pinned back with a plain iron pin, shortened hard every time the composition beneath the house changed and the mark had to be re-cut, which on that road is roughly every second winter. She has never grown it long, and has given one reason each time, and the reasons have all been plausible and none of them has been the truth, which is that long roots give the colony somewhere to finish and she found out what that meant at fourteen.
appearance.marks: The sternum root, settled and quiet. Tracery from wrists to shoulder on both arms and a band across the collarbone, heavier than a lone colony lays and symmetric in a way a paired body's never is. A throat node flattened into the line of the neck. And at the door she keeps, a cut threshold mark renewed every second winter, which is the only public record her household keeps of its own circumstances.
appearance.palette: Bleached scrub linen and sun-brown leather with iron at the pin and the buckles, and the single colour on the whole body a deep black-green in the tracery and across the throat. The rule is absolute: nothing green on any garment, ever, because the one time a visitor's house gave her a green dye as a courtesy she kept the cloth and did not wear it and nobody has ever understood why.
appearance.presentation: A household on the scrub road reads as one large woman with a quiet chest, and that reading is correct without being complete. She is tall, weathered past her actual age, with a settled heaviness in the shoulders that two decades of carrying does and one integration does better. The visible marks are a sternum root cluster that has stopped moving because it stopped needing to, heavier black-green tracery than a lone colony ever lays down running both forearms and across the collarbone, and a throat node so flat it reads as a plain throat until somebody puts a hand on it. The boundary between the two halves of her is visible only under instrumentation, and the instrumentation is the one thing in the setting that kills her, so it has never been done.

art.palette_notes: Bleached scrub linen and sun-brown leather, iron at the pin and buckles, and one deep black-green carried only in the forearm tracery, across the collarbone and at the throat. Absolute rule: no green on any garment, ever, and no translucency or glow anywhere — the colony has to read as something under skin, never as a second shape beside her. Scrub road dust is a pale warm ochre and the key light is late and low, so the doorway she stands in throws her own shadow onto the threshold she cut. Cold open shade behind her for depth; nothing in frame should look like magic, because on this body nothing ever has.

canon.first_appearance: First noticed by a guild of threshold builders testing her mark from the other side, who came back and filed a sound report and one unexplained observation: during the test the keeper had answered a question that had not been put, correctly, several seconds before it was asked.
history: Born a commonborn host and implanted at two months, in the rare accident that ends with integration rather than one half winning; she has never known a version of herself in which this did not happen.

Inherited the colony's stop at the eighth gate, and discovered early that the figure governing her ceiling and the figure written down about her personhood were the same figure, decided by the same act, by somebody else.

Was entered as one legal person with the colony in the one jurisdiction that ruled on the pairing, and discovered within a season that the ruling had solved the accounting and abolished her consent: no act affecting the pair now has a second party who can be asked.
Took up a marked threshold on the scrub road, and found that welcome belongs to the mark, so her household's obligations bind her body and every guest is admitted by the door rather than by her.
Passed nineteen years of testing by a guild that measures marks from the other side, including the season she answered a question nobody had put, and has never been asked about any of it.
Has begun keeping a private count of the requests she would have refused, which nobody can audit, which is the only register of her own that the arrangement permits.
canon.lore: A thornhost is the one configuration in which a thornline colony and a host both reach old age, and it is not a designed cross — it is a commonborn host and a colony that completed integration instead of killing each other, which happens rarely and by nobody's intention. The colony wraps the host's twelve ordinary meridians and cannot cross the liver, the first organ large and dense enough to resist it; it has been observed on the far side and stops there. Because the hybrid's qi moves through the colony's tendril layer, the host's own capacity is irrelevant past that point, so the host's ceiling is the colony's ceiling. She could have gone on indefinitely and cannot, and she cannot give the colony up without dying, which is the whole legal problem about treating the pair as one person stated as a number. The boundary between the halves is visible only under instrumentation, and separating the pair to examine it is lethal to both, so no reading of her exists anywhere. Two entangled souls on one meridian set, held stable by integration; the host's soul is legible, the colony's reads as a second presence rather than as an absent. The host has a second channel carrying the colony's read on her own qi that she has never been able to close and has stopped trying to. And the arrangement was made legal: wherever a jurisdiction has ruled on the pairing, the pair is one legal person, because one person has one liability. That ruling is the most consequential courtesy anyone ever extended her, and it worked exactly as intended. It means there is no second party inside her whose agreement could be required, which means nothing done to her or for her needs anybody else's consent — because there is nobody else in there to ask. She is a person by a ruling that made her a resource. And she has since found the one practice in the setting built exactly for that shape of creature: a household marks its own threshold and welcome is a property of the mark rather than of the person who keeps it, so her obligations bind her body and her body answers for her, and the whole arrangement is more reliable than any consent-based door could be because it never has to ask her anything.

personality.summary: Unshakable at a door and absent from her own arrangements. She is the most trusted threshold-keeper on the road and has never once refused a traveller, has never been asked to, and has begun keeping a list of what she would have said. She has made being agreeable into a discipline, because the alternative is to be asked.

relationships.kind: the argument her mark is the losing side of
relationships.note: A record that can be cited against its owner is what one whole camp refuses and the other cannot live without. Her mark is a public, dated, renewable record of a household, cut in front of witnesses and legible from the street, and it is kept by a woman who cannot be asked whether she consents to keeping it.

canon.role_in_story: A house marks its own threshold, renews the mark when the frame beneath it changes, and admits that a marked threshold may hold while the frame does not — because an unwritten law is not a weak law but an absent one, with no dial and nothing to push, so a community that needs a guarantee of welcome has to build one at the door. Welcome in that practice is a property of the mark, not of the person who keeps it: the mark carries the obligation, the obligation survives the household that cut it, and a traveller is admitted because the door says so and not because the keeper agreed. She keeps the best-kept mark on the scrub road and it is the most reliable welcome in the district, and both of those facts are the same fact. The practice protects her almost perfectly and it protects her by making her unnecessary as a party. Every jurisdiction that has ruled on a thornline host made the pair one legal person, because one person has one liability and two people have a dispute — and that ruling solved the accounting by removing the host's standing inside her own body. So the institution that keeps her safe also means nothing done in her name has required her agreement, and the mark at her door promises in her voice for a woman who has never been asked whether she wanted the promise made. The Threshold Builders test every mark from the other side and the mark is worth exactly what the tester finds. She has passed every test on the road for nineteen years and has never once refused anybody anything.

identity.realm: The eighth gate, and the number is the point rather than the limit: it is her colony's ceiling and not her host's, so a frame that could have gone on indefinitely stops at a figure a jurisdiction wrote down when it decided she was one person. The number that governs her ceiling and the number that governs her standing are the same number and they agree, which is the only reason she has ever been able to hold a door.

name: Orla Skell

reference_stats.combat_read: She will not come off the line and she will not be reasoned off it, because the channel that would argue with her is the same one reading the fight. Expect a holder: feet planted, hands open, weight unmoved, taking the first exchange on purpose so the second channel can finish reading. Do not look for the boundary — you cannot find it, and the one test that would locate it is lethal to her, which is the correct target priority and also the correct way to kill her. Pressure her legs and her attention; she has no stamina problem and every problem she has is about where she is standing. If she begins answering before you have finished asking, the fight is already being lost on information.
notes: Model her as one person by law and two presences in fact. Any resolver that reads her as a single will lose the entire point: the ruling is what makes her consent unnecessary.
The closed path is the mind, and it is closed in the colony's own right — a thornhost is the case the Thornline record means when it says a body's liability is inherited rather than authored.
The two-for-one liability is a legal floor: this body produces two dead and one bill, and every death, burial or save screen for her owes exactly that.
Her private count of refusals is not a secret, it is a register, and registers are the thing this setting fights about. A resolver that has her confide it cheaply has undone the arrangement.
She is unaffiliated by household, not by standing: she holds a mark that outlives her household and answers for nobody in it.
strengths: holds a position for an entire shift without fatigue, because the load is carried by a second system inside the same frame
rejects status effects that route through an ordinary meridian, since the routing in her is the colony's and it was never seated in the ordinary way
answers a question before it is finished, which in a negotiation means she is never the second person to speak
cannot be split, panicked or routed by anything that depends on finding a boundary inside her, because there is no boundary to find from outside
takes the least damage of any body on the road for the least work, because a thornhost costs its host a fraction nothing can measure
reference_stats.summary: A body that fights like a siege work rather than a fighter, because everything she is has been routed around a boundary nobody may look for. Two entangled souls on one meridian set, held stable by integration, capped at a number a parasite chose. Her endurance is the highest on the scrub road and her reach is the shortest, and both facts come from the same tendril layer.
weaknesses: stops at the eighth gate permanently, on a routing problem rather than a shortage, so no amount of cultivation reaches past it
cannot be relocated: the whole arrangement is a body and a place, and one of them is not detachable
cannot be examined, so every claim about her inside is uncorroborated and will stay uncorroborated
has no second party whose agreement can be required, so she cannot refuse an arrangement that uses her body
is removed from a fight she loses slowly rather than quickly, because the second system keeps working after the host has stopped
cannot survive the separation of the halves, which makes every engagement with her a hostage problem she has to win tactically

appearance.age: Unrecorded, and unrecordable in the ordinary way. A body that has held nineteen gates has been alive longer than the frame the ladder describes, and the third name she has worn is not hers either: the second Unwritten who ever lived could not be written down either, so there was one of her, and the name went with the body when the body stopped, and nobody on the ground was willing to be the one who gave it away.
appearance.attire: Clean undyed cloth, one garment, closed at the throat, changed when it is worn out rather than when it is a season. It has been replaced nineteen times and every replacement was bought by somebody else at a shop she was walked to, and the two most recent replacements are the same cut because the shop had the cloth and she had no opinion about it and was not asked for one.
appearance.bearing: Standing absolutely still in a way that reads as composure and is in fact an absence of any mechanism that would move her — she does not fidget, does not shift, does not look away and does not lean. Two witnesses have described her as the calmest person they have ever stood next to. A third described the same stillness as being in a room with something that had decided not to be a person for the duration.
appearance.build: Every organ the ladder requires, and more of each than the ladder defines. She is dense and long and stands very straight without effort, and the only thing anyone has ever found remarkable about it is that she does not tire — which has been recorded as vigour by three witnesses and as the absence of a stable weakness by a fourth, all of whom were describing the same hour.
appearance.complexion: Unchanged. She has no sun line, no scar, no weathering and no age in the face, and this is not preserved youth; it is a body that is inscribing the description it is being given and cannot produce the wear the description implies. Under instrumented light the skin reads one shade in the shadow of a hand and another where the hand is not, and the difference is measurable and does not correspond to anything.
appearance.eyes: The single most-cited unreliable feature in the record. Every account of what she perceived agrees that she perceived everything, which is exactly what a body with no unspent capacity for interior would appear to do to somebody standing in front of it. Her gaze is level, wide and completely unreactive, and the setting's one method for counting what a frame has actually seated has never been run on her because a reading is a description and a description is a charge.
appearance.hair: Dark, uncut for as long as anyone can attest, and blunt-ended rather than grown out, which is the detail every witness agrees on and none can explain: a hair that has stopped growing in a body where everything else keeps going. It is bound back in a single cord and it is the only object in the setting that has been described as hers by three separate observers who were not introduced.
appearance.marks: Nine. Each one is a short line of script laid on the inside of a wrist, added at a different date by a different hand, and every one is a name somebody put on her. She has asked for nothing to be added since the seventh and has been described, correctly, as being difficult about it. The lines do not fade, do not scar, and are slightly warmer to the touch than the skin around them.
appearance.palette: Undyed cloth the colour of weak tea against her own skin, with nothing on her and nothing she has been given that she chose. The only colour anybody has ever put near her is what the reader's plate and the recording light produce, and both of those have ended badly. No ornament, no dye, no pattern; a body that inscribes should not be dressed in anything that inscribes.
appearance.presentation: Described only from the outside, and only by witnesses who were also describing an event, because that is the only condition under which an Unwritten has ever been witnessed and the setting has exactly one of her. Tall, and carrying more of every organ the ladder requires than the ladder defines, which reads as health and does not: she has the frame of something that could be measured twice and came out different each time. What a witness actually sees is a woman in clean undyed cloth standing too still, with a face that agrees with any description of it offered afterwards, and the specific unsettling fact that every report of what she perceived agrees that she perceived everything at once.

art.palette_notes: Undyed weak-tea cloth against skin that is two different shades inside and outside a shadow, and nothing else. No ornament, no dye, no pattern anywhere in frame: a body that inscribes must not be dressed in anything that does. The only marks are nine short lines of script inside one wrist, slightly warmer than the skin around them, and they are the subject of the art rather than a detail of it. Key light flat and unforgiving so that a hand's shadow genuinely changes her colour, warm bounce off a stone floor from below, background a pale field with no depth cue. No glow, no aura, no halo, no inner light — the setting has nothing on her that is magic, and the picture should refuse the reader the comfort of it.

canon.first_appearance: First entered any record as a correction rather than as a person. A reader at a settlement funeral read her off the plate, and the reading was correct, and the body being read did not survive the entry: the charge for the description went into her the way a gate does, and the office's own practice — which keeps the divergence rather than resolving it — meant the divergence it recorded was a divergence in her.
history: Came into being where a life's law runs above the ceiling the world was written to, so the frame accepted every gate it was offered and could satisfy none of them, and there is no record of the place because a description of the place would have been a charge on her.
Reached the seventh gate without anyone teaching her, because a body that inscribes what it is told does not need instruction and does not know that it has been learning.

Was written into a household register on the strength of a plate reading, and the requirement that entry wrote into her could not be met, and that entry is the entire reason she is still alive: nothing else in the setting holds an over-inscribed body in the world for long.

Has attended eleven settlement funerals in three years and asked the Field Registry to read her, because a reading is the only procedure available that produces a second copy of a person, and she has never once concealed what the copy costs.

Received the ninth name, cut into the inside of a wrist by a hand that apologised, and has refused every line since — a refusal that is indistinguishable, from outside, from a body nobody has ever been.
Has worked out, from the outside, that her life is the running sum of every description ever filed about her, that she is owed exactly one more, and has begun choosing which reader gets it.
canon.lore: An Unwritten is a body holding more life than its world's law has room to inscribe, produced when a life law runs above its authored ceiling of one, so the law has no slot in which to write the form down and the form is written anyway. Every gate it passes writes a fresh requirement into the body, and the body cannot satisfy it, because its life law has no slot to hold it; the accumulated contradiction finally exceeds what any frame will bear at the twenty-ninth gate, and the thirtieth would resolve all of it at once. Nobody has returned to describe the thirtieth and the record does not speculate. It has been seen to have every organ the ladder requires and to be carrying more of each than the ladder defines. Its senses are unreliable in the exact shape of the problem: every report agrees that it perceived everything, which is what a body with no unspent capacity for interior looks like from outside. Its diet is not recorded and the only reliable datum is that one has been observed for the better part of a year. Nothing is known about its reproduction and there is one, as far as anyone can tell. It does not spread and it does not persist. Here is the fact its name is about, and it is the same fact its mechanism is about. A law inscribes by writing a requirement into the thing it is written on — and every written account is exactly such an inscription: a name, a lineage, a contract, a reading off a plate, a line in a register, a mark on a grave. The species does not persist because nothing holds it in the world, and it is still here because her name has been written on her wrist nine times and every one of those lines charged her and kept her in existence at the same time. So the record is the only thing making her real and the only thing making her die, and they are the same act done by the same hand. She has done the arithmetic on this from the outside, which is the one thing her own anatomy cannot do, and has concluded that her life is the sum of every description anybody has ever filed, that she is owed exactly one more, and that the twentieth is the one she will not survive. Every account of an Unwritten in the setting is second-hand, because an Unwritten cannot supply its own testimony: observing its own state would be one more requirement with no slot, and the mind path is closed for that reason alone. So there is a body in the setting whose existence rests entirely on other people's paperwork, whose paperwork is the instrument of its death, and which has never once been asked what it would prefer, because asking it would be a charge.

personality.summary: Deliberate, unhurried, and entirely without the apparatus for knowing how much she has spent. She has organised her existence as an accountant would organise a very small reserve: every proof she needs costs, every proof is somebody else's to make, and she has decided that the last one will not be spent by accident. She is the calmest person any witness has stood beside, and every witness has been wrong about why.

personality.voice: Level, unhurried, and almost entirely interrogative. She asks more questions than she answers, and the questions are always about the record rather than about the person: who is keeping it, on what, at whose expense, and whether they have considered what filing it will do. She does not describe herself and has not been asked to by anyone who got that far. Her register has one oddity every witness records: she uses the passive for herself and the active for everybody else, so she is described in her own speech as having been read rather than as having read anything.

relationships.kind: the one office that would enter her correctly, and the reading is the injury
relationships.note: The college reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers, and keeps no second copy because a second copy would be a second opinion. It is the most honest instrument in the setting and it would read her without inventing anything, which is precisely why the reading would be the accurate charge that ends her.

relationships.kind: the one run that counted every frame and could not count this one
relationships.note: The census ran the composition method once across every frame anybody could reach, and its whole value is that it counts what a frame has seated rather than what its tier allows. An Unwritten seats more than the table can hold and has no slot in which to write the difference down, so the one survey in the setting that would have produced her number produced no line for her at all.

relationships.kind: the office whose only certification is the reading that would cost her
relationships.note: The mortal office certifies a breakthrough by taking a reading against the tier's ceiling from an outsider, keeps the list of what was attempted and what the frame read, and has no note of what was felt. It is the correct instrument for a body like hers and she has declined to be inside the ring while it operates.

relationships.kind: the only resource in the setting worth nothing before its owner is
relationships.note: A broken frame is worth nothing before its owner is identified and unmatchable afterwards. She is worth nothing before she is observed and possibly nothing after, which is the same property with the observer moved into the middle of the transaction — and the eleven readings she asked for were eleven attempts to be worth something before somebody decided it.

relationships.kind: the only substrate in the setting that can hold a self larger than its container
relationships.note: Broken law is the only thing that can host a frame above the authored ceiling, which is why three attempts have ever been possible there and fewer have ever been survived. She is in it because a fragment is the one place on the tier where the table has already stopped constraining anything, and because the ring asks for no reading.

relationships.kind: the law table she is the standing argument against
relationships.note: Every gate an Unwritten passes writes a fresh requirement into a body with no slot to satisfy it, and that is the gate mechanism stated as a fact about the ladder. She is the setting's standing argument that the table is a hard limit and not a suggestion, and she is the argument, not the test: nothing in the world will re-open the table to check.

canon.role_in_story: The Field Registry is a mortuary college and it keeps the burnt list: at a settlement funeral the dead are read as the frame said, not as the village remembers, and the divergence between the two is recorded rather than resolved. It exists because the record of a life is also the record of a gate the person was never issued, and it keeps no second copy, because a second copy would be a second opinion. She is the first body in the setting that office would read exactly right. That is the whole of her and it is the reason she is in danger. An Unwritten's frame writes a new requirement into itself for everything it is described as and has no slot to satisfy it, so a plate reading of her is not a measurement — it is a charge. Every institution in the setting keeps its accounts in writing: the Saltledger's standing weight, the Registry's list, the tally the crews read, a contract, a lineage, a grave-marker. She cannot be entered in any of them without being charged by all of them, and the accumulation of charges is the ceiling. So the setting's most honest instrument would kill her correctly, at the correct gate, with a correctly signed reading. She has spent three years attending settlement funerals and asking the college to read her, because that is the only procedure in the setting that produces a second copy of a person, and she has understood precisely what each copy costs. She is the one body whose existence has to be paid for in requirements, every time, in writing, by somebody else.

identity.realm: The nineteenth gate. Seven of the gates above her were reached by somebody writing her down and not one by her doing anything, which is the shape of the whole species: an Unwritten's frame inscribes what it is described as and then cannot satisfy what it has just inscribed, and a body that has never been described has never been charged, so she was six gates clear before anybody in the setting agreed to write the first line down.

name: Hesper Vail

reference_stats.combat_read: Expect no resistance, no fatigue and no pattern, because there is no interior mechanism producing any of those: every report agrees she perceives everything, and that is what a body with no unspent capacity for interior looks like from outside. Do not hunt for a weakness; there is one shape of problem here and it is an inconsistency rather than a gap, and it does not repeat. Pressure her with variety rather than force, because anything that works will work identically the second time and she does not learn. Above all, do not try to confirm what she is — every measurement taken is a description, and a description is a charge, and you would be doing to her the one thing in the setting nobody is permitted to do to her deliberately.
notes: Model inscription and gate as the same operation. If a resolver treats a reading as information rather than as a charge, every one of this character's costs inverts.
The closed path is the mind, and it is closed because observing her own state would be one more requirement with no slot to hold it. Never write it as a temperament.

Her status in the bible is unknown rather than active, on a single witness account of a single event, and the thirtieth gate is genuinely undescribed. Do not resolve either in her favour and do not speculate about the thirtieth.
She is not a boss. There is no fight on her that ends in anything but an accumulation, and a resolver that wants a climax should give her a list of readers instead.
The species does not spread and does not persist. The only reason she is here at all is that nine people wrote her name on her, and each of those lines is on the wrist in the portrait.

reference_stats.summary: The most capable body in the setting and the one that cannot be allowed to be measured, because being measured is the same act as being charged. She exceeds the authored ceiling at every point the ladder offers, has no stable weakness but an inconsistency, and reaches further than anything on record — and every scrap of proof any of it is real arrives as a description, which writes a requirement into a frame with no slot for it.
